## Renal-replacement-therapy (RRT) family -- section-header policy

### RRT_CRRT_EFFLUENT_FLOW (**canonical for total effluent flow rate of a continuous-RRT circuit**)
- **Description:** Total effluent flow rate leaving a continuous / extended renal-replacement circuit -- the sum of spent dialysate, substitution (replacement) fluid, and net ultrafiltration. This is the standard clinical "CRRT dose" metric, normally prescribed weight-normalized in mL/kg/h and recorded absolutely in mL/h. It is the circuit OUTPUT, and therefore distinct from the circuit INPUTS `BFR` (blood flow into the filter) and `DFR` (dialysate flow into the filter): in a hemodiafiltration modality the effluent exceeds the dialysate inflow by the ultrafiltration and substitution rates. Because solute removal by a continuous modality is effluent-flow-limited for small, minimally protein-bound drugs, the effluent flow rate is the natural covariate on an extracorporeal clearance arm; the sieving / saturation coefficient that converts it into a clearance is absorbed into the estimated clearance parameter (`lcl_crrt`) rather than being applied to this column.
- **Units:** mL/h
- **Type:** continuous
- **Scope:** general
- **Reference category:** n/a -- enters as a through-origin linear ratio `(RRT_CRRT_EFFLUENT_FLOW / ref)` or a power-centered ratio on the CRRT clearance arm, and is meaningful only while `RRT_CRRT_ACTIVE = 1`. Reference values observed: 2000 mL/h (2 L/h; Zurawska 2026, the value the CRRT clearance estimate is standardized to).
- **Source aliases:**
  - `FLOW` -- Zurawska 2026 Eq. 6 notation.
  - `EFFLUENT_FLOW`, `Q_EFFLUENT`, `EFR`, `QEFFL` -- printed forms appearing in adjacent critical-care CRRT popPK literature. None was adopted as the canonical: the RRT section-header policy requires the `RRT_<MODALITY>_<KIND>` shape (operator ruling 2026-08-28).
  - Weight-normalized prescriptions (`mL/kg/h`) are NOT this column -- multiply by body weight on ingestion and record the conversion in `covariateData[[RRT_CRRT_EFFLUENT_FLOW]]$notes`.
- **Example models:** `Zurawska_2026_piperacillin.R` (through-origin linear ratio on the estimated CRRT clearance arm, `cl_crrt <- exp(lcl_crrt + etalcl_crrt) * (RRT_CRRT_EFFLUENT_FLOW / 2000) * RRT_CRRT_ACTIVE`, so the 3.4 L/h population CRRT clearance is the value at a 2 L/h effluent flow; the cohort mean effluent was 2.75 +/- 1.1 L/h, i.e. 32 +/- 7.8 mL/kg/h), `ButraguenoLaiseca_2024_meropenem.R` (founding example; supplies the denominator of the effluent-concentration observable of a five-matrix meropenem model in critically ill children on CKRT, `Ceffluent <- cl_hemodialysis * Cc / (RRT_CRRT_EFFLUENT_FLOW / 1000)`, the division by 1000 converting mL/h to the L/h in which the clearance is expressed. Cohort total ultrafiltration rate median 1,253 mL/h, IQR 335-1,870 (Table 2); per-filter mean effluent flows 44 / 60 / 46 mL/kg/h for the low / medium / high surface-area filters (Table 3)).
- **Notes:** Distinct from `QBL` / `QEFF`, which are extracorporeal CLEARANCES in L/h -- `Zhang_2025_fluconazole.R` supplies `QEFF` as effluent flow ALREADY multiplied by a sieving coefficient, whereas this column is the raw prescribed flow with the sieving absorbed into the estimated parameter. Distinct from `Q_CVVH`, which is scoped to a CVVH filter placed parallel to an ECMO circuit (Ahsman 2010 cefotaxime). Distinct from `URINE_FLOW` (native urine output). Pair with `RRT_CRRT_ACTIVE` as the on/off gate; a model that instead derives the extracorporeal clearance from circuit flows via the Michaels equation should use `BFR` / `DFR` and an estimated `lkoa` rather than this column. Note that `BFR` and `DFR` are canonically mL/min because intermittent-hemodialysis circuits are prescribed in mL/min, whereas continuous modalities are prescribed in mL/h or mL/kg/h -- each canonical follows its own modality's clinical convention, so converting between them requires care. Registered 2026-08-28 per operator sidecar ruling covering three tasks that requested the same concept (Zurawska 2026 piperacillin, Butragueno-Laiseca 2022 piperacillin, Butragueno-Laiseca 2024 meropenem); the concept had been encountered before without a column (see the `FILT_SA_MED` Notes, which record that Butragueno-Laiseca 2025 tested effluent flow and could not retain it alongside filter size).

## Renal-replacement-therapy (RRT) family -- section-header policy

### RRT_CRRT_EFFLUENT_FLOW (**canonical for total effluent flow rate of a continuous-RRT circuit**)
- **Description:** Total effluent flow leaving a continuous / extended renal-replacement-therapy circuit -- the sum of the dialysate leg, the substitution (replacement-fluid) leg and the net ultrafiltration -- in mL/h. This is the flow of spent fluid carrying drug out of the hemofilter, and it is the quantity papers report as the "CRRT dose" when normalized to body weight (mL/kg/h). Time-varying in principle; commonly recorded as one prescribed value per patient per session. A FLOW, not a clearance: the drug removed per unit time is the effluent flow multiplied by the sieving / saturation coefficient, so the effluent flow is an upper bound on the extracorporeal clearance rather than the clearance itself. Zero in subjects not receiving continuous RRT.
- **Units:** mL/h
- **Type:** continuous
- **Scope:** general
- **Reference category:** n/a -- enters observation and clearance equations directly rather than as a centered covariate effect.
- **Source aliases:**
  - `phi_Effl`, `phi_Effluent` -- Butragueno-Laiseca 2024 Methods, Base population model, equation 5 notation for the "total effluent flow".
  - `Qeff` -- Butragueno-Laiseca 2024 Discussion prose ("the total effluent flow rate (Qeff)"). NOTE: this paper-side abbreviation must NOT be adopted as the canonical, because `QEFF` is used elsewhere in the pharmacometric literature for an extracorporeal CLEARANCE in L/h (see the `QBL, QEFF` discussion in the Notes below).
  - `effluent flow`, `total effluent flow rate`, `CRRT dose` -- prose forms; when a paper reports mL/kg/h, multiply by body weight to obtain this column.
- **Example models:** `ButraguenoLaiseca_2024_meropenem.R` (founding example; supplies the denominator of the effluent-concentration observable of a five-matrix meropenem model in critically ill children on CKRT, `Ceffluent <- cl_hemodialysis * Cc / (RRT_CRRT_EFFLUENT_FLOW / 1000)`, the division by 1000 converting mL/h to the L/h in which the clearance is expressed. Cohort total ultrafiltration rate median 1,253 mL/h, IQR 335-1,870 (Table 2); per-filter mean effluent flows 44 / 60 / 46 mL/kg/h for the low / medium / high surface-area filters (Table 3)), `Zurawska_2026_piperacillin.R` (through-origin linear ratio on the estimated CRRT clearance arm, `cl_crrt <- exp(lcl_crrt + etalcl_crrt) * (RRT_CRRT_EFFLUENT_FLOW / 2000) * RRT_CRRT_ACTIVE`, so the 3.4 L/h population CRRT clearance is the value at a 2 L/h effluent flow; the cohort mean effluent was 2.75 +/- 1.1 L/h, i.e. 32 +/- 7.8 mL/kg/h).
- **Notes:** Named to the `RRT_<MODALITY>_<KIND>` section policy that heads the RRT family, joining `RRT_HEMODIAL_STATUS`, `RRT_CRRT_STATUS`, `RRT_HEMODIAL_ACTIVE` and `RRT_CRRT_ACTIVE`; the shorter proposals `EFR` / `EFFL_FLOW` / `Q_EFFL` / `QEFFL` / `Q_EFFLUENT` / `CRRT_EFFLUENT_FLOW` were all rejected for breaking that shape. Distinct from `DFR`, which is the DIALYSATE leg only -- the founding source reports dialysis flow (400 mL/h, IQR 150-1,000) and substitution flow (50 mL/h, IQR 50-140) separately from the total ultrafiltration rate, so `DFR` recovers neither the total nor a fixed fraction of it. Distinct from `BFR`, the blood flow entering the circuit. Distinct from `Q_CVVH`, which is explicitly scoped to a CVVH filter placed parallel to an ECMO circuit. Distinct in kind from the `QBL, QEFF` entry, whose `QEFF` member is an effective on-therapy CLEARANCE in L/h: a flow and a clearance differ by the sieving coefficient and are not interchangeable, which is why the paper-side `Qeff` abbreviation was not adopted. Pair with `RRT_CRRT_ACTIVE` to gate the extracorporeal arm off during interruptions. Ratified 2026-08-28 per operator sidecar ruling applied jointly to `oare_ButraguenoLaiseca_2022_piperacillin` (q1), `oare_ButraguenoLaiseca_2024_meropenem` (q1) and `oare_PMC12888853` (q1).

## Hematology

### PLT (**canonical for platelet count**)
- **Description:** Circulating platelet (thrombocyte) count from a complete blood count, typically as a baseline (pre-treatment) covariate but usable as a time-varying value in models that track thrombocytopenia. Completes the routine-haematology covariate family alongside `HGB` (hemoglobin), `NEUT` (absolute neutrophil count) and `WBC` (total white blood cell count). Distinct from a modelled platelet *state*: in semi-mechanistic myelosuppression / platelet-dynamics models the circulating-platelet compartment is a dynamic ODE state, whereas `PLT` is a measured per-subject input column supplied in the event dataset.
- **Units:** 10^9/L (equivalently 10^3/uL, the US reporting convention; numerically identical). Document per-model via `covariateData[[PLT]]$units`.
- **Type:** continuous
- **Scope:** general
- **Reference category:** n/a -- used in centred-deviation form `(PLT - ref)`, in centred-and-scaled form `(PLT - ref) / scale`, or in power scaling `(PLT / ref)^exponent`. Reference values observed: 200 x 10^9/L with scale 100 x 10^9/L (Fukae 2024 valemetostat exposure-safety models; the rounded median and standard deviation of the 102-patient R/R NHL safety analysis set, whose reported median is 194 x 10^9/L and SD 111 x 10^9/L).
- **Source aliases:**
  - `PLT` -- the standard clinical / NONMEM abbreviation; used in `Fukae_2024_valemetostat_plt_decrease.R` (Fukae 2024 Table 1 and Table 3 row `Platelets: 100 x 10^9/L increase`). No value transformation.
  - `BPLT` / `PLTB` -- common NONMEM spellings when the column is explicitly the pre-treatment baseline value.
- **Example models:** `Fukae_2024_valemetostat_plt_decrease.R` (founding example; centred-and-scaled `(PLT - 200) / 100` entering a Bayesian logistic exposure-response model for grade >= 3 platelet-count decrease, both on the logit intercept (odds ratio 0.230 per 100 x 10^9/L increase -- the largest single covariate effect in the paper) and on the unbound-AUCss exposure slope (1.14)), `Stitt_2026_tranexamicAcid.R` (median admission platelet count, reference 196 x 10^9/L; exponent +0.468 on TXA clearance -- the largest of the three clearance covariates in that model, and the one the paper credits with outweighing allometric scaling in the paediatric extrapolation because the paediatric virtual cohort's 205-433 K/uL range sits well above the adult median).
- **Notes:** General scope because platelet count is a routine clinical-laboratory measurement that recurs across oncology, haematology and anti-infective populations, and is the natural haematology sibling of the already-general `HGB`, `NEUT` and `WBC` entries. The bare `PLT` spelling (rather than a `PLT_BL` baseline-marked form) was ratified by operator decision on 2026-08-28 (task `oare_PMC11494914`, sidecar request 001, answer A): the `_BL` suffix in the existing `HGB` / `HGB_BL` pair specifically denotes *initial-condition use for a turnover-model state*, not merely "measured at baseline", so a `PLT_BL` name here would have carried a different meaning from its apparent `HGB_BL` parallel. Register a separate `PLT_BL` canonical if and when a platelet-turnover model needs a per-subject initial condition for a platelet ODE state. Distinct from `PRIOR_SPLEN` (splenectomy indicator), which modulates platelet lifespan mechanistically rather than supplying a count.

## Hematology

### PLT (**canonical for platelet count**)
- **Description:** Circulating platelet (thrombocyte) count from a complete blood count. Baseline or time-varying; document the time resolution per model in `covariateData[[PLT]]$notes`. Used both as a hematologic covariate on drug disposition and as a marker of coagulation-system status in trauma, cardiac-surgery, oncology and hepatology cohorts. In severe traumatic injury an elevated admission platelet count marks an intact (or reactively-activated) hemostatic system, and it predicts faster clearance of antifibrinolytics.
- **Units:** 10^9 cells/L (numerically identical to `K/uL` and to `10^3 cells/uL`; the three labels encode the same value). Document the per-paper reporting label via `covariateData[[PLT]]$units`.
- **Type:** continuous
- **Scope:** general
- **Reference category:** n/a -- used with power scaling `(PLT / ref)^exponent` or linear-deviation forms. Reference values observed: 196 x 10^9/L (Stitt 2026; the centring constant printed inside Equation 1. Note that Stitt 2026 Table 2 gives the TAMPITI cohort median admission platelet count as 197 K/uL -- a 0.5% discrepancy against the equation's own divisor, resolved in favour of the printed equation).
- **Source aliases:**
  - `PLT` -- the universal clinical and NONMEM abbreviation; used as-is in Stitt 2026 Table 1 / Table 2 and Equation 1.
  - `PLTC`, `PLAT`, `THROMBO` -- longer spellings seen in some control streams and lab-extract column headers. Same orientation, no value transformation.
  - `K/uL` -- a *unit* label, not a column name, but it appears often enough in publication tables that it is recorded here: `K/uL` values are already on the canonical `10^9 cells/L` scale and must NOT be rescaled.
- **Example models:** `Stitt_2026_tranexamicAcid.R` (median admission platelet count, reference 196 x 10^9/L; exponent +0.468 on TXA clearance -- the largest of the three clearance covariates in that model, and the one the paper credits with outweighing allometric scaling in the paediatric extrapolation because the paediatric virtual cohort's 205-433 K/uL range sits well above the adult median), `Fukae_2024_valemetostat_plt_decrease.R` (founding example; centred-and-scaled `(PLT - 200) / 100` entering a Bayesian logistic exposure-response model for grade >= 3 platelet-count decrease, both on the logit intercept (odds ratio 0.230 per 100 x 10^9/L increase -- the largest single covariate effect in the paper) and on the unbound-AUCss exposure slope (1.14)).
- **Notes:** Ratified 2026-08-25 alongside the Stitt 2026 tranexamic-acid extraction (task `oare_PMC12794529` sidecar request-001 question q1, answer A), which is the first nlmixr2lib model to consume a platelet-count covariate column. The bare-name form follows the register's established convention for routine clinical analytes (`ALB`, `CRP`, `CREAT`, `HGB`, `WBC`, `RBC`, `HCT` are all bare names at general scope) and the drop-the-`BL`-prefix convention documented under `IL6` -- baseline-vs-time-varying status belongs in per-model notes, not in the column name. `Jiang_2023_imatinib.R` carries a placeholder `PLT` entry in its own `covariateData` that predates this registration and describes itself as having "no canonical register entry"; that note is now stale and the entry can be reconciled against this canonical when that file is next touched. Distinct from `WBC`, `RBC`, `HGB` and `HCT` (the other CBC components) and from `NEUT` / `LYMPH_ABS` (differential subfractions of `WBC`) -- platelets are a separate cell line with separate kinetics. Distinct from `FIB` and the other entries under **Coagulation / hemostasis biomarkers**, which are plasma protein activities rather than a cell count, and from `MPV` (mean platelet volume, not registered) which is a per-platelet size measure rather than a count. Platelet count is time-varying and therapeutically targeted in thrombopoietic and myelosuppression models; the *observable* platelet-count state predicted by such a model belongs in `compartment-names.md`, not here, so a model that both takes admission platelet count as a covariate and predicts a platelet-count endpoint should read this column for the covariate and use a state name for the endpoint.
